title: Adobe makes first tennis move with Australian Open deal
article_text:
Software giant Adobe has made its first entry into tennis through a multi-year partnership with the Australian Open Grand Slam.

Under the deal with Tennis Australia, the company has been named the tournament's official AI marketing and creativity partner.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Through the tie-up, Tennis Australia will utilize Adobe CX Enterprise, an end-to-end platform for customer experience orchestration, to enhance fan experiences by delivering more personalised and connected interactions.

The Australian Open will become Adobe’s first tennis sponsorship globally.

Alan Sharvin, Tennis Australia chief technology officer, said: “One of our core ambitions is to better understand our audiences and deliver more connected, relevant and personalised experiences at scale, whether you’re a fan, a patron or a participant.

“Adobe is a key partner and enabler in helping us bring that ambition to life, connecting our data and digital capabilities to create more value from every interaction.”

With Adobe CX Enterprise, Australian Open attendees will be connected with relevant matches, dining options, and activities, based on their specific needs and interests.

Beyond the tournament itself, the expanded partnership will support Tennis Australia’s digital ecosystem and fan engagement plans.

The partnership will also support the governing body’s global growth strategy, enabling content and campaigns to be tailored for international audiences.

Duncan Egan, Adobe’s vice president of enterprise marketing in Asia Pacific and Japan, said: “The Australian Open is one of the world’s most innovative and iconic sporting events, making it the ideal partner to showcase how AI can transform fan engagement at scale.

“We’re excited to use this platform to reach millions of tennis fans around the world, deepen our connection with customers and communities, and demonstrate how we bring creativity, marketing and AI together to turn ideas into meaningful impact.”

The deal expands Adobe’s stable of sports partnerships and comes soon after it announced a similar deal with North American ice hockey's NHL.

In March, the major software firm renewed and expanded its long-running agreement with Major League Baseball. The company is also a sponsor of American football's NFL and English soccer's top-tier Premier League.

Adobe becomes the second new sponsor of the Australian Open this month after food delivery service DoorDash.

Earlier this year, luxury fashion brand Hugo Boss was brought in as the tournament’s official lifestyle outfitter.

title: CONMEBOL adds Libertadores rights deals with Globo, Paramount+ in Brazil
article_text:
CONMEBOL, South America’s governing body for soccer, has expanded the visibility of its top-tier Libertadores men's club competition in Brazil after securing new rights deals with media heavyweights Globo and Paramount.

The body’s agreement with commercial broadcaster Globo will see the CONMEBOL Copa Libertadores return to its pay-TV service, SporTV, with 41 matches per season, including the final, while Paramount will also show the same number of fixtures and the final on its streaming service Paramount+ live for the first time.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Specifically, the pair’s Libertadores rights bundle (Package C) includes selected matches from the preliminary phases, 24 group-stage matches, two Round-of-16 matches, one quarter-final, one semi-final (shared), and the final (shared with all other broadcasters).

The package also includes coverage of additional CONMEBOL competitions, including the women’s Libertadores Femenina, Libertadores Sub-20 (under 20s), the men’s and women’s Futsal, beach soccer’s Libertadores Fútbol Playa, and esports tournament eLibertadores.

The agreements were brokered by sports marketing agency IMG, which extended its commercial, sponsorship, and media rights partnership (operating through its joint-venture subsidiary FC Diez Media) with CONMEBOL through 2030.

Juan Emilio Roa, commercial director at CONMEBOL, said: “The renewal and return of historical partners is a testimony to the value of CONMEBOL Libertadores to the Brazilian Market and to CONMEBOL's continuous approach in building long-lasting, mutually beneficial relationships with all its partners.

“We look forward to yet another successful cycle with Paramount+ and this expansion in our existing relationship with Globo.”

For Globo, the new deal adds to its Libertadores coverage in Brazil for the 2027-30 cycle, having retained exclusive free-to-air rights to the competition in a deal struck last December.

Under the deal, Globo will keep the games on its digital channel GE TV on YouTube, which launched last year, guaranteeing access to the competition both on television and online.

Fernando Manuel Pinto, sports rights director at Globo, said: “It is with great satisfaction that we further strengthen our partnership with CONMEBOL, an organization that has demonstrably invested in and bolstered its tournaments year after year.

“This new agreement builds upon the one we concluded with the organization last year, bringing more matches, content, and opportunities.”

The main Libertadores rights package in Brazil for the 2027-30 cycle is held by Disney-owned sports broadcaster ESPN, which will have priority in choosing matches each round.

For the secondary Copa Sudamericana, Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) has acquired rights on free-to-air television, with Disney securing the main pay-TV package.

The Recopa Sudamericana, which is contested by the winner of the previous year's Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana, will be broadcast by Globo and ESPN.

title: DAZN builds on NBA, FIBA deals, with Basket.TV acquisition
article_text:
Global sports subscription platform DAZN has bought up basketball streaming service Basket.TV, which mainly serves Latin America.

Basket.TV operates primarily across Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, and Ecuador, and covers both domestic leagues from those countries, as well as a selection of competitions from across the globe.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

This move from DAZN comes after that service – through its Courtside 1891 specialist basketball site – covered the FIBA Women's World Cup, exclusively worldwide.

Courtside 1891 moved exclusively to DAZN earlier this year, having been carried on a non-exclusive basis since 2024. The product had been previously broadcast as a standalone offering on DAZN's platform, not connected to the remainder of its sports offering.

DAZN has also been a joint venture partner of basketball's global governing body FIBA, through FIBA Media, since 2016.

In addition, DAZN and numerous teams from the top-tier NBA have entered into local rights tie-ups over the last few weeks and months – including the Indiana Pacers, Detroit Pistons, Cleveland Cavaliers, Orlando Magic, San Antonio Spurs, Memphis Grizzlies, and Minnesota Timberwolves.

Shay Segev, DAZN Group's chief executive, commented: "This acquisition significantly strengthens our global basketball and supports our broader growth ambitions across Latin America. Together, we'll continue to create great value for fans, leagues, and partners, while continuing to grow the sport around the world."

Latin America is a priority growth market for DAZN – currently, the sports subscription heavyweight is only active to any significant level in Brazil, but is now looking to expand beyond that single market.

In terms of other recent DAZN activity, meanwhile, late last week, a global renewal was unveiled with Extreme H, off-road motor racing’s hydrogen-powered series.

Basket.TV, meanwhile, presently covers around 4,900 basketball matches – in total – each season, for more than 300 teams.

title: Bayern Munich and fintech partner Adyen renew partnership
article_text:
Financial technology platform Ayden will continue as a sponsor of Bayern Munich after extending its deal with the German soccer heavyweights.

Through the renewal, unveiled today, Amsterdam-based Adyen will remain the team's exclusive payment solutions partner.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The Bundesliga champions have had a partnership in place with the company since 2023, through which the brand has been managing Bayern's payment processing across all points of sale for the last three years.

The existing tie-up has an estimated value – by GlobalData Sport – of $1.5 million annually.

It covers purchases at the club's 75-000 capacity Allianz Stadium home venue in Munich and at official Bayern retail outlets.

In terms of Bayern's recent commercial activity, mid-September saw the perennial Bundesliga winners announce an extension with German pharmaceutical company Ursapharm for another three years.

The extension builds on the pair's original tie-up in 2017 and will see Ursapharm and its Hylo brand continue as a gold partner until 2029.

Bayern also brought in artificial intelligence firm Wonderful as a new club partner last month.

This latest tie-up has been unveiled with the 2026-27 Bundesliga season five matchdays in – Bayern currently sit third in the 18-team table, having won three of their five games so far.

As far as sports sponsorships go, Ayden is also a commercial partner of road cycling's Tour of Britain.

Fast-food chain Five Guys has been named an official commercial partner of American football’s NFL in the UK under a three-year agreement.

The US-based restaurant will serve as the league’s official burger partner in the UK across the 2026, 2027, and 2028 seasons.

title: Hang Seng Bank becomes presenting partner of Hong Kong WTT Finals
article_text:
Hong Kong-based financial institution Hang Seng Bank has signed up as a presenting partner for table tennis' 2026 WTT Finals Hong Kong.

The deal, struck between the bank and World Table Tennis (WTT), the commercial arm of the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), covers the 2026 Finals, taking place at the territory's Kai Tek Arena between December 9 and 13.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The finals will incorporate 16 men's and women's singles players and eight mixed doubles teams.

Hang Seng Bank will engage in a citywide campaign involving interactive games, customer offers, and chances to meet players, WTT has said.

In addition, free tickets will be allocated to "low-income families and elderly people" in the territory.

Credit card holders at Hang Seng Bank – which has sponsored Hong Kong table tennis for well over three decades – will be able to buy tickets during a priority access window as well, in late October.

Jonny Cowan, partnerships director at WTT, commented: "Hang Seng Bank has been a long-term partner of the Hong Kong China Table Tennis Association, and it is a pleasure to collaborate with our association colleagues and the Hang Seng Bank team to connect WTT Finals with Hong Kong communities.”

In mid-September, it was announced that the 2026 Finals will take place at Hong Kong’s Kai Tak Arena – the event was initially scheduled for the Hong Kong Coliseum, but has now been moved to accommodate the latter venue’s shift in approach to hosting more concerts.

Last month also saw the ITTF and WTT unveil a major partnership with the heavyweight agency Infront.

Switzerland-based Infront becomes the worldwide lead agency for WTT's commercial development.

The deal runs through 2034 and covers full marketing rights for the entire range of WTT events, including WTT Finals, Grand Smashes, WTT Champions, WTT Star Contender, and WTT Contender tournaments.

World Table Tennis was established in 2019 to modernize the ITTF's commercial approach.

title: Postcard from Lausanne: What the SportAccord Forum revealed about the future of international sport
article_text:
It’s late on Sunday afternoon when SportsPro pulls into Lausanne on a train from Geneva, which means there’s only one place to aim for: the lake.

Even as the sun is starting to set, there is still plenty of activity on the waterfront. As this correspondent (very) gently jogs along the path, periodically checking Google Maps to make sure he is still heading loosely in the direction of Saint-Sulpice, locals are still out on paddleboards, returning from tennis courts and passing a rugby ball between each other.

They don’t call this the Olympic Capital for nothing. After all, nearly 60 international sports organisations and federations are stationed in Lausanne and the surrounding Canton of Vaud, including the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

Leaders from many of those organisations assembled at the Olympic Museum from 5th to 7th October for the SportAccord Forum, which was rebranded this year from the IF Forum to reflect the broader range of delegates, with destinations and service providers also in attendance for the 20th edition of the event.

After sitting in on sessions, conducting interviews and capturing additional content as the exclusive content partner of the event, SportsPro picks out some of the key takeaways from a productive three days in Switzerland.

The first panel of the Forum put winter sports front and centre on the back of the most geographically dispersed Olympics in history.

Held in February this year, Milano Cortina 2026 saw competition spread across existing venues in clusters throughout Northern Italy to minimise the need for new infrastructure. That helped keep costs down, but it also meant a different experience for athletes, fans and other stakeholders.

After seeing her sport stationed in Cortina, alongside skiing and curling, International Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation (IBSF) president Heike Grösswang looked back positively on the experience, but stressed the importance of ensuring those attending the Games still feel at the heart of the action.

That extended to encouraging officials to walk – rather than drive – back from the sliding centre to soak up the atmosphere.

“It didn’t matter if it was 10:30, 11 o’clock at night, we walked through Cortina and there were fans outside,” she said. “So we all could feel what makes the Olympics special, which is this feeling of people coming from all over the world.”

There wasn’t a spare seat in the house as two senior IOC officials – Christophe Dubi, executive director of the Olympic Games, and sports director Pierre Ducrey – took to the stage to shed more light on the body’s ‘Fit for the Future’ strategy, with federations clearly keen to understand what the changes mean for them.

Published in June following the 146th IOC Session, the strategy includes a new methodology to determine the Olympic programme, which is of particular interest to the IFs, many of whom are reliant on the IOC’s revenue distributions from the Games. Speaking on the opening day of the Forum, IOC president Kirsty Coventry said the approach provides “a much more precise and evidence-based way to look at the programme”.

Starting from Brisbane 2032, the core programme will be confirmed seven years out from each Games, with disciplines – rather than sports – assessed against their global appeal, cost and operational complexity, and athlete representation. Meanwhile, sports that drop off the programme will have an opportunity to be reinstated in the next cycle, while accompanying measures are designed to soften the financial blow for affected federations.

Some of the finer details are still to be worked out. But with Coventry saying previously that Brisbane will have fewer than the 36 sports featuring in LA, there was a sense that change is coming.

Prior to the Forum, the IOC published its Trustworthy AI Framework for the Olympic Movement, providing principles and tools that organisations can use when developing or using artificial intelligence (AI) systems, covering areas like safeguarding, data protection and reliability.

That very much set the tone for the three days in Lausanne, where there was unsurprisingly an acknowledgement that AI is not something that federations can afford to ignore. It was fitting, then, that one session was dedicated to technology, offering IFs some practical advice on how best to approach it.

While many sports leaders are embracing AI for personal use, what quickly became clear is that the pace of organisation-wide adoption varies between federations. But what if an AI strategy doesn’t start with AI at all?

That was the argument put forward by Sanjit Atwal, co-founder of sports data agency Halfspace.

“If AI is the car, data is the fuel,” he said. “AI doesn’t work without data. There is nothing for it to generate. There is nothing for it to reference against.

“So AI is not your strategy. It is an output of your strategy towards a defined outcome.”

Atwal, whose background is in ecommerce, did not mince his words when asked whether sport has effectively exploited its data in the past, arguing that the industry in general has done “an atrocious job” and is well behind other sectors.

Atwal advised that federations won’t feel the benefits of AI unless they have a robust data strategy underpinning it. Once those foundations are in place, AI can take on analysis that would otherwise be arduous to do.

“Data collection now shouldn’t be a scary thing to any IF, whatever size,” Atwal said. “It’s cheaper than ever to collect data. We have fantastic frameworks on which to do this.

title: FUEL expands global footprint with acquisition of sports marking agency 53Six
article_text:
FUEL, Ireland’s leading experience and entertainment group, has announced the acquisition of 53Six, the Dublin and London-based sports marketing agency.

Under the terms of the agreement, 53Six will continue to operate under its existing brand identity as part of the FUEL group, led by co-founders Tom Fox (CEO) and Marcus McDonnell (COO).

53Six joins FUEL, the multi-award-winning global group operating across live experiences, creative, employee experience, and high-end content production. Headquartered in Dublin with dedicated teams across the US and UK, FUEL operates on an international scale, delivering more than 650 experiences and events across 55 cities worldwide for a client portfolio that includes PayPal, Coca-Cola, Google, Meta, Airbnb, Universal Music Group, World Rugby, and Amgen. Founded in 2013 by Jamie Deasy and Brian McDermott, FUEL also operates major cultural festivals, including WellFest, Beyond the Pale, and Kaleidoscope festival, the latter in partnership with Festival Republic, Live Nation, and MCD.

FUEL’s global reach spans landmark cultural and sport experiences, including last week’s U2’s 50th-anniversary celebration in partnership with Universal Music Group and Principle Management, the AI-powered fan village at the Amgen Irish Open, World Cup fan zones for Budweiser, global conferences for Coca-Cola, and the Irish premiere of Gladiator II. Named Experiential Agency of the Year at the European Agency Awards and ranked number one agency in Ireland by Eventex, FUEL is also the official Irish member of 27Names, Europe’s leading live experience agency collective.

Founded in 2016, 53Six is a full-service sports marketing and growth agency spanning strategy, creative, content, performance media, and data. The agency’s client portfolio includes some of the biggest brands and rights holders in world sport including Arsenal, Juventus, FAI, Leinster Rugby, the IRFU, Jacksonville Jaguars, Flutter and UEFA.

The agency’s recent work demonstrates its ability to turn strategy and creativity into commercial results. For TEG Sport, full-funnel digital media strategies drove multiple sell-out fixtures, including a record attendance for the Irish women’s rugby team’s first game at the Aviva Stadium. For Betfair, 53Six delivered a fully integrated World Cup campaign in Spain fronted by brand ambassador Luis Figo. Its continuing partnership with Leinster Rugby combines powerful storytelling with the implementation of a new customer data platform to deepen fan loyalty and drive commercial growth throughout the season.

The deal reflects a defining shift across the global entertainment industry: live experiences, sport and culture are converging around fandom, participation and community. By bringing these worlds together, the partnership creates a model built for where the market is heading; one that combines the power of live experiences with the ability to build audiences, deepen fandom and create lasting commercial value.

Speaking on today’s announcement, FUEL Co-Founder and Managing Director Jamie Deasy, who was recently named one of Europe’s top 50 Event Agency Leaders, stated: “We’re delighted to welcome 53Six into the FUEL group. We’ve known Tom, Marcus, and the team for some time, and there’s a very strong cultural fit and shared ambition between our two companies. 53Six brings deep expertise in sport, performance marketing, and audience intelligence, while FUEL brings scale across live experiences, entertainment, and high-end content production. Together, we are building an end to end global growth engine for clients around fandom, combining world class live experiences and content with the fan-data and insight to demonstrate their impact, while creating significant growth opportunities for both businesses internationally.”

Tom Fox, Co-Founder and CEO of 53Six comments: “We were looking for a strategic partner that understood how sport and live experiences are increasingly interconnected, and could further accelerate our growth internationally. Since day one, we’ve believed in the power of sport to create meaningful shared experiences, and in today’s world, that belief feels more relevant than ever.”

Marcus McDonnell, Co-Founder and COO of 53Six adds: “Our capabilities are highly complementary: 53Six brings the sharp end of sports marketing, FUEL brings scale across experiences and high-end production, and together we share expertise in content and creative. That’s a genuinely different proposition for the industry and we are excited to join the FUEL group for this next chapter.”

Headquartered in Dublin with teams across the US and UK, FUEL is a multi-award-winning global group operating across live experiences, creative, content, and employee experience, and high-end production, and major cultural festivals including WellFest, Kaleidoscope, and Beyond The Pale. Ranked number one in Ireland by Eventex and named Experiential Agency of the Year at the European Agency Awards, FUEL delivers activations globally for clients including Google, Meta, Coca-Cola, PayPal, Universal Music Group, Amgen and World Rugby.

Founded in 2016, 53Six is the growth agency for sport, combining creative content, performance media, and fan data analytics to drive commercial revenue for rights holders and global brands.

Co-founders Tom Fox (former Setanta Sports and Twitter) and Marcus McDonnell (former NBA and Pitch International) bring deep sector authority in sports technology, digital business, and media rights. They are backed by a team of 20 specialists across performance analytics, strategy, creative, content, and digital product management.

53Six’s client portfolio includes Arsenal, Juventus, UEFA, IRFU, and Leinster Rugby.

title: Brands, betting and broadcast models: What to watch at Sportel Monaco 2026
article_text:
For more than three decades, Sportel Monaco has been where the sports media business goes to do deals. Rights holders, broadcasters, streamers and the technology firms that sit between them descend on the Grimaldi Forum each October to buy, sell and size each other up.

That part isn’t changing. With the exhibition floor already 80 per cent sold out and more than 80 exhibitors expected, the 2026 edition is shaping up to be as busy as ever. Industry heavyweights including Relevent, Two Circles, Infront, LaLiga, the National Football League (NFL), Fifa, ESPN, Sportradar and Deltatre are among those already confirmed to attend, while the usual suspects like YouTube, JioStar, Warner Bros Discovery, AWS and IMG are also set to be part of the mix.

What is changing, however, is who else is in the room, and what they want to talk about.

The biggest structural addition this year is the CMO Brand Programme, a full day of closed-door panels and curated networking taking place on Monday 19th October and run in collaboration with Qualcomm, the programme’s main sponsor.

The idea is simple, if overdue. Sportel has always been a media rights and distribution event. Brands have tended to arrive late to the party, once a rights deal is done and it’s time to buy inventory or sign a sponsorship.

This year, however, organisers want to bring them in much earlier – into conversations about content, audiences, data, and how a sports property’s value is built in the first place.

The timing is deliberate. With the traditional rights model under pressure in parts of the market, sponsorship and brand partnerships are carrying more of the commercial load. Sportel’s pitch is that those revenue lines should be developed together rather than in separate rooms.

The line-up gives the concept real weight. Ashish Babu, chief marketing officer at Tata Consultancy Services, whose sports portfolio runs from major marathons to Jaguar TCS Racing in Formula E, is joined by Revolut’s Rory Miller Cheevers, Diageo’s Paddy Carberry, who heads up sport for Guinness and its Premier League and Six Nations partnerships, and Qualcomm’s Garret Ponder, who leads brand partnerships for a Snapdragon portfolio that includes Manchester United.

Fintech, IT services, drinks and chips: four very different categories, all betting heavily on sport. Elsewhere another session will discuss sport and brands as a two-way growth engine, while RTL AdAlliance chief executive Stéphane Corbule leads a discussion on rethinking sponsorship for an age shaped by media, technology and content.

The organisers are candid that this first edition of the CMO Brand Programme is a starting point rather than a finished product. But if it works, it could reshape what Sportel is for.

On the main Speakers Stage, the headline act is LaLiga president Javier Tebas, who will sit down for a keynote interview on the league’s next moves in broadcasting.

Expect talk of new distribution models, partnerships and format innovation, as well as piracy and audience fragmentation – two subjects Tebas has never been shy about.

Few executives in European soccer generate as many headlines, and fewer still are as willing to say what they think in public.

The conference is anchored by four masterclasses, each tackling a pressure point for the industry.

The first, on the new global sports ecosystem, looks at how consumption is going global, how businesses are moving from direct-to-consumer models towards more interconnected B2B2C setups, and how investors judge opportunities across the value chain. Deltatre chief revenue officer Peter Bellamy, IMG’s Hillary Mandel and Bruin Capital founding partner Jeff Roth will share their perspectives in what promises to be a useful discussion on the convergence of technology, rights and capital.

Meanwhile artificial intelligence (AI) gets its own session, of course, with the emphasis firmly on moving from experiments to full-scale use.

SVG’s Ken Kerschbaumer leads a panel featuring JioStar’s Prashant Khanna, BuzzMyVideos chief executive Paola Marinone, Ekstraklasa’s Marcin Serafin and SURJ Sports Investment chief executive Danny Townsend. Governance, IP, rights and trust are all on the table.

Production is next. After an Olympic Games and a Fifa World Cup that showed top-tier coverage no longer needs hundreds of staff on site, SVG Europe’s Will Strauss asks what comes next. On that, Bundesliga Media’s Dominik Scholler, TNA Wrestling president Carlos Silva, LiveU’s Sarah Jakob and Protocol Sports Marketing’s Lowell Conn all weigh in.

Finally, live betting. Bolt6 chief executive Steve Carter, AWS’s Paul Devlin and Sportradar’s Patrick Mostboeck will dig into the technology behind in-play wagering, and the thorny issues of latency, integrity and regulation that come with it.

If one company is making a statement in Monaco this year, it’s YouTube.

The platform has three dedicated sessions. Jonny Keogh, head of UK sports, will make the case for putting YouTube at the centre of rights holders’ distribution strategies. Pedro Pina, YouTube’s vice president for EMEA, joins LiveMode partner Thiago Tourinho and media analyst Evan Shapiro to unpack how LiveMode broke World Cup broadcast records, and what creator communities and brand partnerships mean for live sport. A third session with sports executive Jason Wachs is still to be detailed.

For an industry still working out how far to lean into free, creator-led platforms, those sessions could be among the most useful of the week.

Elsewhere, case studies from Deltatre (World Athletics), Pixotope (BBC Sport), ViewLift (Fisu) and the Esports Foundation (Warner Bros Discovery) sit alongside sessions featuring Mediapro, Dolby OptiView, Wurl, Epic Clips, Grey Matter Entertainment and the XR Sports Alliance, plus the Pitch Perfect Innovation Contest.

title: Sky Sports partners with Mental Health Foundation
article_text:
Sky Sports has partnered with the Mental Health Foundation to deliver a mental health awareness campaign marking World Mental Health Day on 10th October 2026, combining personal storytelling with practical resources to encourage conversations about mental wellbeing.

The initiative features two short films, including one starring Sky Sports pundit and former England international Paul Merson, who speaks openly about his experiences with mental health and suicidal thoughts.

The campaign aims to use the visibility of sport and the reach of Sky Sports to help audiences engage with mental health issues, while providing information about where to access professional advice and confidential support.

Merson’s involvement brings a personal perspective to the initiative. Having previously discussed his struggles publicly, the former Arsenal midfielder uses the film to share his experiences with viewers, highlighting the importance of speaking about mental health and seeking help.

The partnership also places an emphasis on practical support beyond awareness-raising. Sky Sports has signposted audiences to resources from the Mental Health Foundation, alongside services including Samaritans, SHOUT and NHS mental health support.

The campaign reflects the growing role of sports broadcasters in addressing wider social issues through their content and talent. By placing a familiar football personality at the centre of the initiative, Sky Sports is seeking to make conversations about mental health more accessible to audiences who might not otherwise engage with the subject.

For the Mental Health Foundation, the collaboration provides an opportunity to reach sports audiences through one of the UK’s largest sports media platforms, extending the visibility of its work beyond its existing channels.

The initiative also demonstrates how sports media partnerships can combine editorial storytelling with public health messaging, using personal experiences to encourage discussion while directing viewers towards established support organisations.

World Mental Health Day is observed annually on 10th October, with the 2026 campaign forming part of wider efforts across sport and society to promote mental health awareness, reduce stigma and improve access to support.

title: Do you really know your supporters?
article_text:
Discover how rights holders are building a Single Supporter View in our live webinar on Wednesday 14th October at 3pm.

How well do clubs really know their supporters? As supporter interactions become increasingly fragmented across ticketing, memberships, retail and digital channels, many organisations are looking to build a more complete picture of the people they serve.

Join Data Talks and Bradford City AFC for an open webinar exploring how rights holders can build a clearer view of their supporters and turn that understanding into more relevant and engaging experiences.

You’ll hear directly from Bradford City AFC about their journey towards creating a Single Supporter View, while Data Talks will share how clubs can use supporter insight to drive engagement, improve personalisation and unlock commercial opportunities.

The 45-minute session will explore the challenges created by fragmented supporter data, what a Single Supporter View looks like in practice, and how better supporter insight can improve outcomes across ticketing, memberships, retail and sponsorship. Attendees will also gain insight into the role automation and AI can play in supporting ongoing supporter engagement and more personalised fan journeys.

Whether you’re looking to strengthen supporter relationships, improve the effectiveness of your marketing and communications, or better understand how data can support commercial growth, this webinar will provide practical examples and actionable insights.

Register now to join the conversation and hear directly from those putting these principles into practice.

title: Shorts: Millwall FC, Footballco, For The Love Of Rugby
article_text:
Millwall FC has announced a new partnership with Trustee Fire & Security Ltd, expanding an existing relationship with the South London and Kent-based company that dates back to 2018.

The agreement will see Trustee become the Championship club’s fire safety partner, increasing its branding presence at The Den and providing further opportunities to engage with Millwall’s business community.

As part of the partnership, Trustee will receive branding on fire-exit signage at several exterior locations around the stadium, alongside sponsorship of the communal bar area within the club’s newly refurbished hospitality boxes.

The two organisations will also collaborate on initiatives to promote Trustee’s services to businesses connected with the club over the coming seasons.

Founded in 1978 as Trustee Alarms, the company is headquartered in Orpington and provides fire protection, security and life-safety services across London and the South East.

Its services include fire detection systems, CCTV, access control, intruder alarms and passive fire protection, working with clients including local authorities, schools, housing providers and commercial organisations.

The agreement formalises a longstanding relationship, with Trustee having supported Millwall through both sponsorship and work undertaken at the stadium since 2018.

Luke Wilson, Chief Commercial Officer at Millwall, said, “Maintaining relationships with the businesses that have supported the club for so long is just as important as introducing new businesses to the excitement of a matchday at The Den. We’re excited to start a new chapter with Trustee and look forward to working even more closely with the business across the rest of the season.”

Nick Toomey, Company Director at Trustee Fire & Security and a lifelong Millwall supporter, said, “This partnership gives us a fantastic platform to showcase Trustee Fire & Security and the business we are today, while continuing to strengthen our association with the club.”

The deal strengthens Millwall’s portfolio of regional commercial partners while providing Trustee with greater visibility through stadium branding and access to the club’s corporate network.

Football media and culture company Footballco has appointed Charlotte Thomson as Head of Women’s Football and Culture, strengthening its leadership team as it looks to expand its global women’s football portfolio.

Based in London, Thomson will oversee strategy, content development, commercial growth and brand positioning across Footballco’s dedicated women’s football platforms, including INDIVISA, Yalla Girl in the Middle East, and US brands Soccer Girl and No White Shorts.

The appointment comes as Footballco looks to capitalise on the growing commercial opportunities surrounding women’s football, with a focus on building audiences and connecting brands with the sport’s expanding fanbase.

Thomson joins from The ONE10 Collective, the agency she founded, where she worked with organisations including Glasgow City, the Women’s Regional Leagues and the Women’s Sport Trust.

She previously served as Head of Women’s Football at Copa90, bringing experience across football media, content strategy and the wider culture surrounding the women’s game.

In her new role, Thomson will lead the development of new content formats across Footballco’s existing platforms, alongside exploring opportunities to establish additional brands within its women’s football portfolio.

Stefano D’Anna, President of Footballco, said, “Charlotte not only brings her experience of women’s football content and strategy to this role, but also a deep understanding of the culture that surrounds the sport. This is vital not only for our own growth, but also for our partners who value insight, authenticity and cultural relevance to engage this growing fandom.”

The appointment comes ahead of the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, although Footballco has emphasised that its investment in women’s football extends beyond the tournament.

Charlotte Thomson said, “While everyone is focused on next year’s Women’s World Cup, for us our investment goes far beyond the tournament. INDIVISA has always been about more than what happens on the pitch, so I’m looking forward to growing the brand’s impact in culture, showing more diversity in our storytelling and continuing to champion the mantra of ‘More Women in Football’.”

Footballco’s approach reflects the increasing importance of culture-led content within women’s football, as media companies seek to develop audiences and commercial partnerships beyond traditional match coverage.

JAECOO UK has renewed its sponsorship of For The Love Of European Rugby for a second season, extending its partnership with the rugby content platform ahead of the new European club rugby campaign.

The agreement will see the automotive brand present 16 episodes covering the Investec Champions Cup and EPCR Challenge Cup, as the competition builds towards the 2027 finals in Lyon.

The renewal follows a previous season of collaboration between JAECOO and For The Love Of Rugby, which included a branded road trip to Bilbao for the 2026 European finals weekend in a pink JAECOO 7.

The new agreement will increase the partners’ investment in club rugby content, with coverage beginning during the opening round of European competition.

For JAECOO, the sponsorship provides an opportunity to connect with rugby audiences through digital content and the personalities associated with For The Love Of Rugby, rather than relying solely on traditional sports advertising.

The partnership also reflects the automotive brand’s continued use of sport and entertainment to build its profile in the UK market.

For The Love Of Rugby has positioned its European coverage as an extension of its wider rugby content offering, using its digital platforms and social media presence to engage supporters throughout the club season.

The renewed collaboration will again bring JAECOO branding into the coverage of both European competitions, with the partners indicating plans to build on last season’s activations as the tournament progresses towards Lyon.

title: beIN SPORTS secures Wimbledon broadcast rights
article_text:
beIN Asia Pacific has secured exclusive broadcast rights to Wimbledon across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong from 2027 to 2031, extending its long-standing media partnership with the All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC).

The five-year agreement will see live coverage of The Championships distributed through beIN SPORTS and its streaming platform, beIN SPORTS Connect, across ten markets, including Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Hong Kong.

The deal also covers Brunei, Cambodia, Timor-Leste and Laos, with beIN set to provide comprehensive coverage of the tournament across its linear and digital platforms.

For the London-based AELTC, the agreement represents a further expansion of Wimbledon’s international media distribution, strengthening its reach across Asian markets through an established regional broadcaster.

The partnership builds on beIN’s existing relationship with Wimbledon, following the recent extension of its broadcast rights across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) through 2030.

beIN also holds exclusive Wimbledon rights in France and broadcasts all four Grand Slam tournaments across MENA, making tennis a significant part of its international sports rights portfolio.

Mike Kerr, Managing Director of beIN Asia Pacific, said, “Tennis is a key pillar of our portfolio, and we have continued to grow audiences by bringing fans closer to the sport’s biggest tournaments, players and moments. This agreement reflects our long-term commitment to the sport and our shared ambition with the AELTC to build on Wimbledon’s strong connection with audiences here, deepen engagement across the region, and drive the next phase of growth together.”

Paul Davies, Associate Director, Broadcast, Production and Media Rights at the All England Club, said, “Welcoming Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to beIN’s portfolio marks an exciting new chapter in our relationship. By leveraging the strength of beIN’s premium linear channels and advanced digital platforms, we look forward to deepening fan engagement, growing audiences, and bringing the unique magic of Wimbledon to more tennis fans across Asia than ever before.”

The agreement reinforces the commercial importance of international broadcast rights to Wimbledon, while providing beIN with another major property as it develops its premium sports offering across Asia.

title: LTA commits £1.6m to university tennis and padel
article_text:
The Lawn Tennis Association has announced a £1.6m investment in British university tennis and padel through to the end of the 2028/29 academic year, representing a 15% increase on its previous funding cycle

The funding will be match-funded by participating universities, unlocking a further £1.6m and bringing the combined investment to £3.2m over the three-year period.

The LTA also plans to expand its network of partner universities from 32 to 50 nationwide by the end of the funding cycle, increasing opportunities for student participation, workforce development and competition.

The investment will prioritise programmes designed to grow tennis and padel participation among students and local communities, alongside initiatives supporting the development of coaches, administrators and facility managers.

It will also support improvements to university competitions, with tennis remaining one of the largest sports within British Universities and Colleges Sport (BUCS). A total of 391 teams have entered BUCS tennis competitions for the 2026/27 season.

Will Roberts, CEO of BUCS, said, “We are delighted to see the ongoing investment of the LTA into University Tennis through to 2029. This investment provides BUCS member universities the confidence that they are making a difference to participation levels and supporting the development of the next generation of leaders in the sport.”

The funding builds on recent developments in university tennis, including the introduction of a BSc Applied Sports Studies in Tennis degree at Leeds Beckett University and the inaugural BUCS Padel Championships.

British student tennis has also enjoyed success internationally, with the national student team winning gold at the Master’U Championships in France.

Beyond competitive performance, the LTA is placing greater emphasis on universities as a pathway into employment and volunteering within the sport, helping students gain experience that can support tennis and padel clubs after graduation.

Alistair Higham, LTA Universities Manager, said, “University tennis has gone from strength to strength in recent years, both in terms of players’ on-court performances and their off-court involvement and impact in clubs nationwide upon leaving university.”

The expanded funding programme forms part of the LTA’s wider efforts to strengthen the long-term development of tennis and padel across Britain, with universities playing a growing role in participation, education and workforce development.

title: How the Man City cheating scandal created a geopolitical minefield
Andy Burnham’s own goal
Private equity puts string of UK high street names up for sale
Russia ‘interfered’ in 2016 Brexit vote, says Andy Burnham
A tale of two possums
Points pile-ups, old-school Saracens and a royal pint
article_text:
It is worth taking a step back to fully appreciate the scale of scoring in the Prem currently.

Ten seasons ago Northampton hosted Bath in round three.

As on Saturday, Saints won to end Bath's unbeaten start to the season. The score then was 24-6.

Northampton scored four tries - from Courtney Lawes, George North and David Ribbans (twice). Bath had only two penalties from Rhys Priestland to show for their visit.

This weekend it wasn't just a different game. It was like a different sport.

Between them the teams scored 18 tries en route to a ludicrous 71-48 scoreline.

The 119-point aggregate score was the second highest in English top-flight rugby history, beaten only by Northampton's 94-33 win over Bristol in May.

Those two games are part of a recent trend.

Five of the 10 top-flight games to have breached the 100-point barrier have come since the start of the 2023-24 season.

Looking back at that round of games from 2017-28, there were 26 tries in total across six matches, an average of 4.33 per game.

This weekend there were 50 in five games, an average of 10 per match.

That is an increase on even the first two rounds of this season, which delivered an average of 9.3 tries per game - the highest-scoring start to an English top-flight campaign since data specialists Opta began gathering the statistic in 2007-08.

"The game can be too slanted to attack," Northampton head coach Sam Vesty, whose speciality is attack, told BBC Sport after his side's win.

"I don't want to watch basketball, but we saw some fantastic rugby on both sides."

Vesty believes the current scoring spike is a product of laws of the game and the philosophy of the teams playing it.

"I think officiating [is one factor]," he said.

"The offside line is being reffed hotter; tackle height is lower so therefore people can keep the ball alive more quickly. Then there is the speed of the game - the ball is on a little longer so people are more fatigued.

"I also think there is more intent from teams, going out to score points, when that has not always been the case."

Former England head coach Eddie Jones was always sceptical about how well the Prem prepared players for the grind of Test rugby, where scores are invariably harder earned.

The flip into international action may take some acclimatisation for England's stars this autumn.

It isn't just the throwback kits and spiky presence of Brendan Venter that is giving a retro feeling to Saracens this season.

Defence coach Adam Powell's aim at the start of the season was not just plug some holes, but change the way the game is played in the Prem.

He told his players he wanted Saracens to challenge the dominance of attack and make defence a hallmark of the team, just as it was in their heyday last decade - the Wolfpack reformed.

They have started the season well on that front.

Only Gloucester have conceded fewer points, and keeping previously unbeaten Bristol to just seven points in a 30-7 victory was Saracens' most impressive defensive display of the season.

There was a heft to Sarries' pack with new signing George Martin paired with 6ft 9in prospect Olamide Sodeke in the second row and Maro Itoje, looking revitalised after his summer break, impressing at blind-side flanker.

Owen Farrell piloted the hosts well from fly-half, bringing his accuracy as well as his usual intensity.

Saracens' most destructive defensive force at home, though, might go unseen.

Bristol rested three players - Pedro Rubiolo, AJ MacGinty and Steven Luatua – because of concerns about their bodies, external holding up to playing on the artificial surface at the Stonex Stadium.

The Bears are not the only club who will avoid selecting players, external with particular injury histories on artificial surfaces.

With Newcastle's pitch having been relaid over the summer, and Gloucester's first put down in 2021, Saracens' surface is now the oldest of its type in the Prem.

It may be the one area where Saracens will look to the future soon.

After starting Northampton's first two games of the season, scrum-half Archie McParland had a bench role in the win over Bath.

The 21-year-old, who would have toured with England this summer but for lacerated leg suffered in the Prem final win over Exeter, got on for the final 20 minutes against Bath.

Meanwhile, 22-year-old Charlie Bracken got 40 minutes on his first start of the season for Saracens in their win over Bristol, providing speedy service and aiming some well-judged bombs for brother Jack to chase.

However, both McParland and Bracken face formidable roadblocks in the way of more regular game time in the Prem.

British and Irish Lions Alex Mitchell and Tomos Williams are their respective team-mates at Saints and Sarries.

How will their clubs manage their resources at nine? Is it possible to keep everyone happy? Does 20-year-old Lucas Friday, who signed a new contract at Harlequins last month and may see a clearer route into the first team, have an advantage?

It will be intriguing to see how the next generation of England nines plays out.

After a round in which three of the five games finished within a winning margin of seven or fewer points, there is not one unbeaten side in the league.

It is still early days. The form lines are still murky.

title: Exeter examine extent of Feyi-Waboso injury
article_text:
England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury he suffered in Exeter's win over Newcastle.

The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half of the 34-28 Prem win at Sandy Park - Exeter's first of the season.

He has started all three of the Chiefs' Prem games this season - scoring two tries at Bath last week.

He started all three of England's Nations Championship games over the summer and crossed for tries against Fiji and Argentina.

England host Australia, Japan and New Zealand in November in the second half of the competition.

Feyi-Waboso missed this year's Six Nations after hurting his hamstring in January and missed the second half of the 2024-25 season with a shoulder injury.

"It feels like he's overloaded his hamstring a little bit," Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Sport.

"I don't think it's catastrophic, I don't think it's been a proper twang.

"He carried on after he first reported it, had another kick chase, came up with the ball at full speed, chased back but he just doesn't feel right.

"So I expect that'll get scanned and then we'll assess it earlier in the week.

"I would say it's more of a concern than a long-term worry."

title: WRU names businessman Faulkner as new chairman
article_text:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has named former Newport and Ponytpool player Lyndon Faulkner as the governing body's new chairman.

The 66-year-old is the nephew of legendary Wales and Pontypool prop Tony "Charlie" Faulkner and has become a successful businessman in the United States since his playing days.

Faulkner will take over the role vacated by Richard Collier-Keywood at the WRU's annual general meeting on Sunday, 22 November.

He will do so at a time when the WRU is planning to cut the game's professional tier from four to three teams, with west Wales sides Ospreys and Scarlets vying to avoid becoming surplus to requirements.

The WRU has already confirmed the team it owns, Cardiff, and privately-backed Dragons, will continue to exist beyond the 2027-28 season.

The WRU described Faulkner's appointment as "a major coup" and said he can "court the respect of both its community and professional game and the wider business world around it".

In a WRU statement Faulkner said: "This is a pivotal time for the game and I will start by listening to those around me and of course remaining open to credible challenge."

He added: "I know personally how important Welsh rugby is in many different ways to the nation.

"So, it is a huge privilege for me to return to Welsh rugby as chair of the WRU and give something back to a sport which has helped define me and means so much to me, my family, friends and the people of Wales."

The WRU said Faulkner would bring a "fresh perspective" and his mandate, as well as ambassadorial, was to lead strategic direction for the game in Wales and to hold its executive team and staff to account.

WRU chief executive Abi Tierney, who in April 2026 denied Collier-Keywood had been forced out, said: "I know Lyndon and I are ready to form a formidable team working to advance Welsh rugby at all levels."

Faulkner attended Bassaleg Comprehensive School in Newport and played for Newport Youth before going on to figure at centre for their senior side and Pontypool when they were one of Wales' leading teams.

After injury ended his playing days, Faulkner progressed off the field into the corporate world where he has held senior roles including with Technicolor®/Nimbus CD International, Microsoft and Nimbus CD International, Pelican Products and Peli Biothermal.

Faulkner's CV also includes entrepreneur awards and appearing on US TV series 'The Mentor' as well as lecturing at Stanford University Business School and at the University of Virginia's Darden Business School.

title: Wade set to break Prem try-scoring record
article_text:
Newcastle boss Dan McFarland is confident Christian Wade will break Prem Rugby's try-scoring record.

The 35-year-old former England winger scored a hat-trick in Newcastle's 34-28 loss at Exeter to take his tally to 100 over his career.

Wade needs just one more try to equal Chris Ashton's record of 101, which was set in April 2023.

"Christian is a really good man, an excellent connector," McFarland told BBC Sport.

"He'd be in our leadership group because of his capacity to be able to connect with everybody across the squad. He's a really good temperature taker."

Wade scored the bulk of his tries during his seven-year spell at Wasps before leaving rugby union for American football in 2018 as part of their international player programme.

He joined the Buffalo Bills in 2019 and scored a touchdown on his very first play in a pre-season game.

But he did not break into the side's NFL roster and was released in April 2022 where he moved to France to playing with Racing 92.

He returned to England in 2024 with Gloucester and after a short spell joined Newcastle in 2025.

"In terms of what he brings on the field, he's got the dancing feet, he's got the speed and he's got a danger out there that has to be marked," added McFarland.

"For a guy who's not one of the new age of 6ft 3in wingers, he can dominate the aerial battle, so he's done a really good job for us there.

"He obviously brings a lot of professionalism as well from his time in the NFL and understanding of what it is to be a professional athlete.

"It's not just a job, it's a lifestyle and he exudes that."

Having scored a hat-trick against his side, Exeter boss Rob Baxter knows first-hand how tough it is to stop Wade.

"He's still a challenge but to be fair, it's a nicer challenge now than it was a few years ago," he told BBC Sport.

"Fair play to him, now he's still performing well and he's obviously still got a great top-end pace but I think now you kind of know you've got to work together, get across the pitch nice and early.

"I think on the whole we defended him pretty well but I think Newcastle created opportunities for him really well as well.

"It's a hell of an achievement - but I'd have liked him not to have got to 100 tries playing against us today!"

title: Late Sale penalty try continues Harlequins woes
article_text:
Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium.

The Sharks came from behind to win the game with a 73rd-minute penalty try after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to give Quins an early lead.

After their opening-day reverse to Bristol at home, Sale have bounced back strongly with back-to-back wins over Saracens and Quins.

Despite their first points of the season, the loss leaves Quins rooted to the foot of the table.

Harlequins, crushed 48-0 by Gloucester last weekend, were much more resilient and, with Smith involved for the first time this season after a finger injury, much more threatening.

But Sale, while nowhere near their best, fought their way out of a tight corner to record their fifth successive win against Quins in domestic and European competition.

Quins were good value for a 17-14 half time lead, scoring three tries and having two more disallowed by the television match official (TMO).

Hooker Sam Riley gave them a third-minute lead after Smith and George Furbank had combined in midfield. Then Smith finished off some fine approach play from Furbank.

Sale, without Tom Curry who dropped out through illness, struck back with a try of their own from Fijian Elia Canakaivata on his first Prem start before Smith sliced through some poor defence for his second try.

The hosts cut the deficit just before half-time through scrum-half Gus Warr but with the Sharks making too many errors, Riley was mauled over for Quins' bonus-point try in the 53rd minute.

Sale fought their way back through a try by lock Ben Bamber after a break by Nicky Smith and a big line-out steal from Courtney Lawes kept them within striking distance.

And they went ahead after a rumbling maul which took Quins back 30 metres before Riley pulled the ball down close to the try line.

Referee Christophe Ridley awarded a penalty try and sent the hooker to the sin-bin.

There was no way back for Quins who must hope a change of competition to the Challenge Cup next week, with a home fixture against Vannes, brings a change of fortune.

"Fair play to Sale. They got themselves back into the game with their set-piece but I'm really proud of the boys' efforts up here. I'm just happy for the boys that they got some reward out of their work.

"If you're prepared to go to dark places for us and win those collisions, then you're going to get selected. If you're dipping your toe in one week and then not the next, then we can't tolerate that.

"You can't be up one week and then down the next week like we had last week. Performance will dictate the shirts."

"We were chasing the game all day. The fight's in them clearly and it's the second week they've found a way to win.

"They've had to manage the way through games, problem-solve and come up with solutions and that's really rewarding.

"I'm really, really proud of that but we're still not where we want to be in terms of performance because that [chasing the game] won't be good enough against Glasgow next week. We know that - but we'll take this win.

"If you can win playing badly, then that's a good sign. It's up to us to step up, it's all within our hands and our capabilities. That's the exciting bit, isn't it?"

Sale: Carpenter; O'Flaherty, Marchant, Lozowski, Reed; Ford, Warr; N Smith, Jibulu, Opoku-Fordjour, van Rhyn (c), Bamber, Lawes, Tshiunza, Canakaivata.

Replacements: Cowan-Dickie, McIntyre, Francis, Dugdale, Hanson, Louw, Loganimasi.

Harlequins: Furbank; Green, Northmore, Bradley, Murley (c); M Smith, Porter; Hobson, Riley, Kerrod, Dun, Treadwell, Kenningham, Driscoll, Cunningham-South.

Replacements: Walker, Johnson-Holmes, Streeter, Petti, Schmid, Friday, Beard, Isgro.

title: Davies urged to reverse retirement for World Cup
article_text:
Gareth Davies has been urged to rethink his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup by former Wales team-mate Scott Baldwin.

The 36-year-old scrum-half sparked a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down to beat Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday.

Davies retired from Test rugby in 2024 but ex-Wales hooker Baldwin believes the veteran could still thrive at a fourth World Cup next year.

"He could be just what you want in a quarter-final of a World Cup, in a Wales-England fixture in 12 months' time," Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport.

"He's not going to be overawed with the pressure of that environment. And outside of Tomos [Williams] really, have we got the depth there to come on in those huge moments?"

Davies won 77 Wales caps during a 10-year Test career that included two British and Irish Lions tours, a Grand Slam and Six Nations title.

He has since appeared as a regular TV pundit and will be 37 by the time of the 2027 World Cup where Wales face Zimbabwe, Tonga and England in Pool F in Australia.

But Baldwin believes Wales coach Steve Tandy should consider a conversation with Davies because of his World Cup know-how.

"It's just it's one more year and it may not mean playing in the autumn [Nations Championship] or Six Nations. It may be, look, 'come World Cup time, I know what you can do, I want you to be part of the squad'," said Tandy.

Davies - the leading all-time Welsh try-scorer in the URC - was a second-half replacement for Dane Blacker against Benetton and helped inspire Scarlets' first win of the season.

"Firstly, he did not look like a 36-year-old, he looked like someone who was out playing his first game - that's how much it meant to him," said Baldwin.

"That was the desperation he showed and the moment when the Scarlets needed it.

"They're 21-7 down, you've got a 36-year-old scrum half coming on and the energy he brought was outstanding. I have no doubt that would have driven the energy of those players around him."

Baldwin also believes Davies' presence could mirror the way South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus utilised Schalk Brits in 2019 after the hooker had retired at Saracens.

Saracens' Williams is Wales' number one choice at half-back with rival Ospreys Keiran Hardy and Reuben Morgan-Williams also in the mix.

He said: "Tomos Williams is out and out number one [but] I challenge someone to show me a better scrum after that than Gareth Davies.

"We're building for a World Cup next next year. I haven't given up hope on [Wales] getting out of the group and getting into the deep stages of the knockouts with the squad."

Baldwin also recalls the 2015 World Cup when Davies scored an iconic Welsh try as they beat England, a result that played a significant part in the hosts' tournament downfall.

"If you look look back to the World Cup I went to. We lost our first choice 9, 15, 10, 12 and had [scrum-half] Lloyd Williams playing on the wing.

"We're a very resilient nation and sometimes we've got to be a little bit smarter on the players we've got.

"We are missing depth in certain areas but if you can get Wales' best 23, fit and healthy and on the pitch, they'll always have a fighter's chance. That's all we really need and all we've probably ever had."

Baldwin's comments were echoed by Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies who hailed the scrum-half's "superb" contribution.

He added: "Gareth has been struggling with having to sit in the wings a little bit because he's such a competitor, but he's getting used to actually contributing in different ways to what he's done in the past and he came on and made a big difference."

title: Wade scores 100th Prem try as Newcastle lose to Exeter
article_text:
Christian Wade became just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter.

Wade, 35, went over twice in the first half - his second giving the Red Bulls a two-point half-time lead - before pouncing on a Henry Slade error to race in for a third early in the second half.

Newcastle's former England winger is now just one try off the all-time Prem try record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023.

Wade, who spent four years trying to break into the NFL from 2018, returned to the Prem in 2024 with Gloucester after two years at French side Racing 92, last year moving to Newcastle after a brief spell at rugby league's Wigan Warriors.

Exeter's Ross Vintcent marked his return from injury with a try after just 38 seconds as the two sides shared five tries in the opening quarter that left the hosts 19-14 up.

While the game did not go on to match Saturday's 18-try, 119-point thriller between Northampton and Bath, it did see eight tries as Slade's 64th-minute penalty and a late Bachuki Tchumbadze try ensured a first win of the season for Exeter.

The bonus-point win keeps Exeter in eighth place in the Prem but closes the gap with leaders Gloucester to four points while winless Newcastle are second-from-bottom having got two losing bonus points.

A sparse crowd of 7,071 – which led to the closure of 15,600-capacity Sandy Park's North Terrace for the first time for a Prem game – watched Exeter make a superb start as Vintcent charged down Zack Henry's kick to go in under the posts.

Those who did attend saw the try-scoring start continue as Wade levelled the score three minutes later - the Red Bulls' winger went in for his 98th Prem try after some excellent Newcastle passing.

Slade was at the centre of Exeter's next two tries, setting up Vintcent for the Italy forward's second in the 11th minute before selling a superb dummy to coast in from 40 metres nine minutes later – but only after Wade had put in Max Hicks to briefly give Newcastle the lead.

Exeter had Ethan Roots sin-binned for a no-arms tackle on Red Bulls full-back Harrison Obatoyinbo 14 minutes from the break and, moments before his return, Wade went in for his second after Sammy Arnold had broken through the Exeter line.

Summer-signing Sam Harris – making his Exeter league debut at full-back – dived in four minutes after the restart to restore Exeter's lead but it lasted just four minutes before Wade raced over from 40 metres for his third score after Slade's wayward pass, reaching his century of league tries.

The hosts thought they had scored a fifth try soon after when Stephen Varney dotted down from close range but replays showed a forward pass from Slade to Harris in the build-up.

Exeter took the lead with 16 minutes left when Slade kicked a 40-metre penalty and the result was secured in the dying moments when Georgian forward Tchumbadze got on the end of a maul from a close-range line-out.

"At half-time, my biggest frustration was with our defensive energy.

"I thought we were attacking pretty well. I thought we looked a lot more enthusiastic in attack.

"I think we knew how to create opportunities to score, which was obviously speed of ball in the middle of the pitch and then getting the balls to wider channels where we could kind of create mismatches and pick off two-on-ones.

"That part of it I was quite pleased with but when we had the ball the other way around, for some reason we were just lacking in energy, drive and speed off the floor, speed to go forward and quality of tackles.

"Fair play to Newcastle, I thought they exploited that quite well because they kept the ball up and alive. They got the ball into space and scored some good tries - that flip-flopping of the score almost wouldn't let us settle."

"Every time you lose, you're disappointed.

"Both weeks I've been proud of a lot of what we've done, very proud of the effort that we put in there, very proud that we went out and played the brand of rugby that we want to play going forward.

"The fact that we've come to last season's finalists and lost narrowly at this stage is at the same time disappointing and positive in knowing that what we're trying to do we're, putting in place."

title: Exeter Chiefs to bolster squad with rising South African lock
article_text:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter is set to bolster his squad after agreeing to sign André Goedhals from Currie Cup outfit the Pumas to strengthen his injury-hit second row.

The second row has been a problem area for Baxter, with Italian star Andrea Zambonin on the sidelines after a shoulder operation. Although he is closing in on a return to action, he could still be weeks away, as is Lewis Pearson.

But he is looking to solve his problem by landing Goedhals, who holds a British passport after being born in Devon while his parents lived and worked in England, making him English-qualified.

Goedhals, 21, returned to South Africa when his family settled in Riversdale, a farming community in the Western Cape, before he finished his schooling at the renowned Oakdale Agricultural High School.

He was highly rated as a schoolboy and won Springbok under-20 honours, but moved to the Pumas after fading and failing to live up to his early promise in the highly competitive Stormers setup.

Goedhals becomes the third member of the Pumas side to move to the Gallagher PREM this summer after lock JJ Scheepers joined Sale Sharks, and prop Sampie Swiegers was snapped up by Harlequins.

Another Pumas ace, flanker Ruwald van der Merwe, has been taken to Scotland by Glasgow Warriors boss Franco Smith, and it continues Baxter’s shopping spree after last week announcing the signing of Carwyn Tuipulotu from Pau under the noses of Bristol Bears.

He hopes to have better luck with Goedhals than with Khwezi Mona, who played only nine games before being released in the summer, along with Kwenzo Blose, who made 24 appearances in two seasons at Sandy Park.

Former Springbok hooker Joseph Dweba, who moved to Devon at the start of last season, is yet to appear for the Chiefs in this campaign despite being in full training.

The Chiefs, who won their first game of the season against Newcastle Red Bulls on Sunday, will also welcome All Black Dallas McLeod from Canterbury at the end of the month after helping them reach the NPC semi-finals, where he scored seven tries in nine games.

title: ‘A great sense of pride’: Alexandra Chambon named France captain for New Zealand tour
article_text:
With Pauline Bourdon Sansus unavailable for France’s three-Test tour of New Zealand, François Ratier has named Alexandra Chambon as captain.

The 26-year-old scrum-half is the team’s third-choice captain, with Manae Feleu prioritising her medical studies and Bourdon Sansus remaining in France this October for personal reasons.

Captain of her club side, FC Grenoble Amazones, in AXA Élite 1, Chambon will lead an inexperienced France team that will also be without Yllana Brosseau, Siobhan Soqeta and Charlotte Escudero.

“First of all, a great sense of pride,” Chambon told France Rugby. “It’s a role that naturally brings that with it. I’m also very grateful to the coaching staff for the trust they’ve placed in me.

“I hope this tour will be just as wonderful as the one we recently had in France, because everything went so well there. My goal is to support everyone as much as possible, since we have a squad that still includes quite a few new faces.”

“I know I’ll be well supported by Gabi [Gabriel Vernier], Annaëlle [Annaëlle Deshayes] and Léa [Léa Champon] — I even room with Léa,” Chambon continued.

“It makes the experience even better to share it with them. I already have plenty of experience playing alongside these players in the matches and competitions we’ve been through together. We get along really well, which will be a huge help in this role, and we’ll be able to support one another.”

France began their WXV Global Series campaign against the Black Ferns in Lyon, losing 28-14 to Whitney Hansen’s side before recording wins against Australia and Canada.

Three more Test matches against New Zealand are sure to test France. The Black Ferns’ last-gasp defeat to the Red Roses at Allianz Stadium was the team’s first loss of 2026 and their first defeat under Hansen.

Facing the second-highest-ranked team in the World Rugby rankings will be a major challenge for France, who are still finding their feet under Ratier, having seen him take charge at the start of the calendar year.

“The goal, obviously, is to go out and perform well away from home against a top-four team,” Chambon said. “We’ve shown that we’re on the right track: we learn from every match, and no two games play out the same way.”

“We will therefore need to adapt and really go out and get results against the top-four teams. New Zealand is one of them; we are set to face them three times, so we have to find a way to beat them on their home turf. That is the goal.”

title: Italy name 30-player squad for WXV Global Series tour of USA
article_text:
Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna has named a 30-player squad to tour the USA for two Test matches against the Women’s Eagles.

The squad includes Michela Sillari, who could earn her 100th Italy cap this weekend in Mansfield, Texas, if selected in the matchday 23. Italy will face the Eagles again a week later in Nashville, Tennessee.

Sciamanna has selected a highly experienced squad for the October WXV Global Series fixtures, with Elisa Giordano (84 caps), Beatrice Rigoni (88 caps) and Sofia Stefan (108 caps) among those included.

There are also three uncapped players in the squad: Benetton Rugby Treviso pair Silvia Fent and Mascia Jelic, and Rubina Grassi of Toulon.

A knee injury has ruled influential loosehead prop Silvia Turani out of the tour, while Gaia Maris, Veronica Madia and Margherita Tonellotto have also remained in Italy to receive treatment for their injuries.

In their September home fixtures in the WXV Global Series, Italy recorded a comprehensive 55-21 victory over Japan before suffering a 41-29 defeat to South Africa in their most recent outing.

title: Ex-Hurricanes Poua coach takes on key Fiji women’s rugby role
article_text:
Former Hurricanes Poua head coach Fusi Feaunati has been named Head of Women’s Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union [FRFU].

The appointment follows growing interest and participation in women’s rugby across Fiji. Currently, 12 teams compete in the Subrails Marama competition, while 16 teams participate in the Royal Tea Ranadi tournament.

Feaunati’s role will focus on connecting the pathway from community rugby to the high-performance programmes of the Fijiana Sevens and Fijiana XVs.

Feaunati said: “What excites me most about this opportunity is the ability to help shape a connected women’s rugby pathway across Fiji, from community and youth rugby through to elite international performance.

“Fiji possesses extraordinary talent, passion, athleticism and cultural strength. With aligned systems, athlete support, coach development and performance planning, I believe FRFU can continue to establish itself as a genuine world leader in women’s rugby.”

Feaunati brings experience across community, development and high-performance rugby. In 2025, he was head coach of the Hurricanes Poua in Super Rugby Aupiki, having previously served as an assistant coach.

His previous roles include women and girls lead with the Wellington Rugby Football Union, coaching positions with Wellington Pride in the Farah Palmer Cup, Black Ferns Wellington hub manager with New Zealand Rugby and development roles with Manawatu Rugby Union.

As Fiji looks to strengthen its national teams, Feaunati will work with high-performance academy staff, provincial and school coaches, and community coaching programmes to establish a sustainable women’s rugby pathway.

“Women’s rugby in Fiji has grown tremendously, and we acknowledge the contributions of players, coaches, schools, provincial unions, families and communities within our rugby ecosystem. But growth also brings responsibility. We now have to make sure the leadership, systems and programs supporting our women and girls grow at the same pace as the game itself.

“This appointment is not simply about one national team or preparing for the next tournament. It is about connecting the entire women’s rugby pathway, from the young girl playing rugby at school through provincial competitions and development programmes to Fijiana 7s and the Vodafone Fijiana XV.

“We recognise that there are gaps and challenges to address, including stronger pathways, better alignment between programmes, continued coach development, appropriate athlete support, clear performance standards and greater accountability.

“Fusi brings experience across those different levels of the women’s game. His role will be to help us bring those pieces together and establish a high-performance environment that is distinctly Fijian, professionally driven and capable of delivering sustainable success.”

title: Tom Willis steps up to dominate Top 14 in Jack's absence
article_text:
Jack Willis may remain sidelined with a leg injury, but his brother, Tom, has ensured that the Willis family continues to wreak havoc on the Top 14.

The 27-year-old continued his barnstorming start to his second life at Bordeaux-Begles with a decisive role in his side’s 23-22 victory over ASM Clermont-Auvergne at the Stade Marcel Michelin on Saturday.

Tom made a match-leading 18 carries in the victory, and came close to scoring a try off the back of a driving maul, only for team-mate Maxime Lucu to take hold of the ball in the process of grounding it. Had the try been awarded to Tom, it would have lifted him to joint top of the try-scoring charts in the Top 14, level with Pau’s Rodrigo Marta with six in the opening six rounds.

On top of his carrying, the former Saracens No.8 produced four turnovers, including a breakdown steal in his own 22 at the death to deliver his side the victory.

Such a performance earned the eight-cap England international a place in both Midi Olympique’s and L’Equipe’s team of the week selections.

Tom’s form in the opening rounds of the French season has ensured there has been no let-up in the Willis domination of the league despite his brother, reigning Top 14 Player of the Year Jack, being absent since round two with a thigh injury.

Jack coincidentally sustained the injury against Bordeaux-Begles, though he shared barely any time on the pitch with his brother as the Toulouse star left the field just over 10 minutes after Tom had come on as a substitute.

Tom will play a vital role in Bordeaux’s attempt to win a third straight Investec Champions Cup title this season. Their campaign gets underway against Gloucester at Kingsholm on Friday, where England fans will get a first-hand glimpse of how the ineligible star is faring with his new club.

title: 'French Paul doesn't miss... I was just wondering what celebration he was going to pull'
article_text:
'French Paul doesn't miss... I was just wondering what celebration he was going to pull'

The opening month of the 2026 Nations Cup delivered a stream of competitive, high-intensity games, multiple outstanding tries and set-piece battles, and several great moments and memories that made July a successful start to the newly formed competition.
